mainEntity.name: Can a home expansion be designed as an in-law suite or accessory dwelling unit?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, you can build an in-law suite or accessory dwelling unit (ADU), provided your property meets local zoning rules and building requirements. Homeowners frequently use expansions for aging parents, returning adult children, or guest suites. The main practical tradeoff involves utility and privacy planning: an attached suite can often tie into the main home's existing plumbing and electrical systems, while an independent living setup may require separate subpanels, independent HVAC, or private exterior entrances. We review these specific use cases during initial consultation to establish the appropriate scope and building design.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes. Expansions can serve as in-law suites or guest quarters, depending on whether you require an attached room or an independent living area with its own utilities and entrance.
